subject: English
passage: "The Lantern and the Wind" is a 1904 poem by Yan Le. In the poem, a lantern is portrayed as intending to confront and resist the wind: ______
prompt: Which quotation from "The Lantern and the Wind" most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "I am the Lantern. Night descends cold; / The howling gusts through the valley rolled; / With icy breath and shrieking cry / They tear my flame and make it die."
choices.B: "I am the Wind. I shape the world / As a potter shapes his clay when hurled; / Mountains bow and forests bend, / Their proud green crowns to me they send."
choices.C: "I am the Lantern, boastful Wind! / I am set here to stand against thy kind. / Rage and roar or whisper low, / I am set to check thy might, and so I shall go!"
choices.D: "I am the Wind. The earth I roam; / Stone to me is drifting foam; / Beneath the sweep of my tireless breath / The cliffs are carved and brought to death."

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. This quotation focuses on the lantern, which addresses the wind directly and announces its intent to "stand against" the wind and "check [its] might." This matches the idea of confrontation and resistance in the claim we're trying to support.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. This choice doesn't illustrate the claim. While this quotation does focus on the lantern, it suggests that the lantern is overwhelmed by the wind — its flame is torn and made to die. It lacks the sense of boldness and strength implied by the phrase "confront and resist the wind."
